findings.reason: In `/[.*+?^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g`, the character class closes after the escaped backslash. The pattern therefore needs a special character followed by a literal `\\]`, which never occurs, so replace() returns the path unchanged before it goes into new RegExp. A path containing `(` or `[` would make the test throw or fail. Only the test is affected.
findings.claim: The regex-escape helper in the missing-script test escapes nothing, so the test breaks on checkout paths that contain regex metacharacters.
findings.evidence: In `expectedScriptsDir.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, "\\$&")` the character class closes at the first `]` after `\\`. The pattern therefore matches one special character followed by a literal `\\]`, which never occurs in a path, so `replace` returns the path unchanged before it is put into `new RegExp(...)`.
